consequences:
You look Sophia in the eye and wish her good luck and safe travels.
There is plenty of danger on the road in Magra — especially now, in these troubled times — but you are confident that Sophia will survive and thrive no matter where she goes.
She nods and looks away.
“Yeah, you’re right. I’ll be okay. You’d better be okay too, <username>. I can’t help you anymore. From now on, you’re on your own.
“Be careful who you trust. And don’t get yourself caught.”

Sophia stands up, slings her bag over her shoulder, and hands you a sheathe. It contains a misericorde — a long, slender dagger.
You accept the parting gift.
A moment later, the door closes quietly behind her.

Only then do you realize that she was waiting for something from you, something more than just a few kind words and a good-luck wish.
But Sophia is gone now. The moment has passed.

You are alone.
Last Straw rests solely on your shoulders now.

You take a step toward her — and kneel.
You swear to remain loyal to Sophia and her cause, forever and ever, no matter what. Until the very end.
Sophia lets out a hard, bitter chuckle — and kisses you, hard and hungrily, biting your lips until they hurt.
She is a force of nature, a calamity, a ruthless, elemental power. Her insistent fingers undo the buttons of your shirt. She does not ask — she just takes. And right now, she wants you.
You follow her lead exactly, undoing the ties of her blouse — but only as long as she permits it. You have no choice but to obey.
Sophia pushes you down onto the floor and straddles you. She does not allow you to move. She does everything herself, as always.

When the sun rises, the two of you are still together. You are exhausted, spent, done. The sweat-drenched scratches left by her nails still sting. 
Nude, Sophia lights her pipe. She does not seem the least bit tired.
Neither of you speaks to the other.

Slowly, Sophia begins sifting through the clothes on the floor.
Once she is dressed, she hands you a sheathe. It contains a misericorde — a long, slender dagger.

“Here. It’ll remind you of your oath.
That was fun, <username>. Don’t miss me, okay? I won’t miss you either.
“There’s so much dirt in our past, and so much blood in our future… but we won’t stop until we’re done. Our cause is just.”

The door closes quietly behind her.
Last Straw rests solely on your shoulders now.
Her eyes narrow.
“Get up! What’s with the noble melodrama?”
“So what if I tell you to go and die for me, eh? True death? Would you still be loyal to me?”

You stand up and take a step closer.
Yes, you tell her. Any order she gives you, you will obey without question. You are completely and utterly loyal to her.

You take her by the hand and kiss her tobacco-stained fingers.
Sophia squeezes your hand so hard it hurts.
“You’ll regret those words someday.

“You’re standing awfully close to me, Brante. Too close, maybe.
“I’ve got nothing to give you, see? You won’t get any tenderness or joy from me. Just rage and revenge.

“You ain’t free until you’re ready to make sacrifices with no regrets. And I’m way past regrets. I’ll sacrifice you too one day.
“You sure you’re ready for that?”

Surrendering to a rush of emotion, you take her by the hand.
No matter where she goes, you will always be on her side. She is more than just a comrade-in-arms — she means the world to you. You will do everything in your power to protect her. She should never forget that.
But before the door closes quietly behind her, you hear an even quieter whisper…
Sophia raises an eyebrow.
“What, you think I need protection? You think there’s something waiting for me I can’t handle?”
You reassure Sophia that she has your complete confidence. There is no need to get upset. But even so, you want her to know that here in Anizotte, she always has someone she can rely on.
“Oh, Brante… you really think I’m that naive? Me, relying on an agent of the Secret Chancellery? Next you’ll tell me I’m gonna dance on the Peak in a white gown after I’m dead!”

You sigh.
Sophia is free to doubt your words if she wants, but right now you are being sincere. And, no matter what she thinks, you will be always be there for her, even if it means defying Felipe’s orders.

Silence follows.
Sophia grins.

“Fine. Hope I won’t be needing your help. But here, have something to remember me by. Maybe it’ll give you some confidence.
“Time for me to hit the road, <username>. You watch your back while I’m gone. Remember — our cause is just.”
She hands you a sheathe containing a misericorde — a long, slender dagger. Then she nods and walks away.

You muster all your courage and take a step forward, as though you are about dive into cold water.
If you are going to be apart for so long… you want her to know something: you have been in love with her ever since you were children.
You remember every moment you spent together. The games you used to play… her escape from the city… your chance encounter in Eterna…

You have both experienced plenty of misfortune in your lives, but you are still happy because you have always been together.
The days you spent with Sophia were the best days of your life. You will miss her terribly.
Sophia rubs her temples, as though unsure of what to say.
“Wow, <username>. It took a lot of guts to say… what you just said. Only a brave man could say something like that right now.

“I wish I could tell you I feel the same way. Believe me, I do. But I can’t. These words, these feelings — we can’t afford them. We need to put everything we’ve got into achieving our goals. Trust me, it’s better this way.

“If I ever need your help out there, I’ll let you know. And… good luck here in Anizotte, <username>. You can do it. You’re a good leader.
“Here, take this to remember me by, okay? Our cause is just.”

She hands you a sheathe containing a misericorde — a long, slender dagger. Then she nods and walks away.
The door closes quietly behind her.
You take a moment to think, then sit next to Sophia. After another pause, you finally speak your mind.

You cannot stop, you do not want to stop, your head swimming in a blissful daze, your mind all but gone, dissolved in those kisses. The warm caresses, so gentle… the whispers, so soft and sweet… the beating of your heart… the sound of discarded clothing falling to the floor…

She is so vulnerable, so amazingly, impossibly defenseless. You never thought she would open herself to you like this, and yet here she is, right by your side, smiling and crying, laughing and kissing, touching and caressing, looking at you so tenderly, all at once.
The night lasts an eternity. You are with her. She is yours.

The sun rises. She has to leave.
You can barely force yourself to let her go. Your kisses follow her to the doorstep. You promise to wait for her. You swear to remain by her side until the very end.
Just before the door shuts, Sophia gives you a sheathe containing a misericorde — a long, slender dagger.
“Here. It’s for you. May it give you strength. You can do anything. I know it. It’s just the way it is.

“That was amazing, <username>… the memory of our night together is the most precious thing I’m bringing with me. It’ll tide me over until I come back to you.
“Take care. And don’t be afraid of nothing. Our cause is just.”

She gives you a long, slow kiss, then leaves at last.
The door closes quietly behind her.
Last Straw is on your shoulders now. But you are no longer alone.

You have had this feeling ever since you were a child. You have tried to fight it, tried to ignore it, but it was all in vain. And now there is no reason to hide it anymore.
You remember every moment you spent together. The games you used to play… her escape from the city… your chance encounter in Eterna…
You have both experienced plenty of misfortune in your lives, but you are still happy because you have always been together.

And then you say it: I love you.
I will always be there for you. I will keep you safe from the rest of the world. There is nothing I will not do for you.

Sophia freezes, as though she has forgotten how to breathe.
She interrupts you in a hushed whisper.
“Why are you… this can’t be happening… this isn’t real, it’s never real — nobody stays, everybody leaves, one way or another… I’m leaving right now… and then… then you’ll leave me too…”

You get down on your knees before Sophia and kiss her tobacco-stained fingers. You embrace her with great care, holding her close, stroking her hair.
No, you will never leave her. Not ever.
Her back grows stiff. But then… Sophia’s shoulders begin to shake. She is crying. Crying… you never thought it possible.

You wipe the tears from her eyes. She holds your face in her hands.
And kisses you on the lips.
There is nothing to say. She feels exactly the same.

053.060.010_EnteringTroops.title: The Legion

buttons.ButtonDescription1: You ask him to violate his order and let the people protest despite the risk of incurring the overseer’s wrath.
buttons.ButtonDescription2: You are prepared to give Tommas the names of the commoners inciting unrest in the city. In exchange, you will recruit several Legion officers as Secret Chancellery informants.
buttons.ButtonDescription3: You start printing leaflets condemning the presence of Gaius Tempest and the Legion in the city.
buttons.ButtonDescription4: You give Tommas the names of the nobles plotting against the overseer in exchange for his assistance.

consequences:
You and Tommas have known each other ever since you were boys.
You used to play on these very streets, pretending to be heroes of old, fighting the great battles of the past.
Now Tommas commands the Legion soldiers sent to Anizotte to quash the unrest, while you command Last Straw and have spent several years preparing the city for a full-scale revolt.
It is not about you, you explain. You want Tommas to hear you out not as a battalion captain, but as your old friend who grew up right here, on the streets of Anizotte.

The power struggle between Gaius Tempest and Tarquinius Milanidas has starved Magra and shattered the lives of many of your friends.
The people are at the end of their rope. They cannot live like this any longer.
They will never stop protesting because their only hope is to get the overseer to listen to them.
The protestors are not a handful of insurgents, you tell Tommas. No, they are all people he has known his entire life, and they are only protesting because they have no other choice.

If the Legion soldiers try to stop them, there will be blood. Tommas will have to slaughter his own people.
You do not want this for him. You do not want this for the people of Anizotte.

“That can’t be, Brante…
“What do you mean, the overseer isn’t listening? That’s why my battalions are here — to bring peace back to the people! To show them the overseer cares about them and wants to protect them!”

Tommas has been away from Anizotte for a long time. The people have grown desperate. They now see Legion soldiers as enemies rather than protectors.
Sooner or later, they will clash. The only way to prevent bloodshed is for the Legion to allow the people to be heard by the overseer.
And the more people assemble, the sooner he will hear them.

“What are you saying? How can you ask me this? I’m here to stop that from happening!
“If I go against the overseer’s orders… why, that’s treason! Do you know what they do to traitors? They’d hang me without a second thought!”

You raise your hands in a conciliatory gesture.
Obviously, you don’t want your friend to be punished. But some things just have to be said. There are so many lives at stake here, and Tommas is in a position to make a difference.
Tommas sighs anxiously, rubbing his forehead.
“You’re right about one thing, <username>: I haven't been back to Anizotte in a long time. I’ll take a look around, see things for myself. And if you’re right… then maybe I’ll think about it.”
There it is, the ruins of Char Milanidas’ palace. The remains of your childhood fort still stand among the crumbling stonework.
Certainly, you reply. That is all you ask.

The city is quiet for the next week. The people slowly grow accustomed to the sight of Legion soldiers patrolling the streets, but remain nervous around them just the same.
A fortnight after the conversation with your old friend, a letter arrives.

“Dear Brante,
“You were right. I spoke with my friends and family, acquaintances, simple folk… and it’s true. They’ve got nothing left but hope.
“I also met with nobles, including the overseer himself, and none of them even want to see how they’re driving the city off a cliff.
“I’m a warrior, not a butcher. I will not allow the Legion to silence the people with steel — no matter what.
It is time to act.

A sea of people fills the Chancellery square.
Legion soldiers stand between the mob and the Chancellery itself. Tommas’s vibrant cloak flashes here and there behind their backs. They stand with their shields together, but their spears are pointed upward rather than at the protesters.
They do not take a single step toward the crowd.

You personally instructed your comrades to make sure the gathering remains peaceful, but you are still terrified to see so many people amassed in one place.
You cannot see Alida, or Fuad, or Oliver… but you hear one voice after another begin shouting from various parts of the mob.
More and more voices join the chant.

“Legion out of Anizotte!
“Legion out of Anizotte!
“Legion out of Anizotte!”

The Legion battalions remain frozen in place, like stone statues.
They do not let the commoners reach the Chancellery walls, but they do not disperse them either.

An hour passes like this. Then another.
The chanting dies down, only to begin again and again.
Father Fuad’s speeches keep the mob on the edge. Oliver’s paid barkers do their job. Alida’s voice stokes the fire in the hearts of the young. But the people are getting tired.

Tommas arrives alone, without any soldiers to guard him.
He wears a suit of armor and the vibrant cloak of a commanding officer, a sword by his side. His shoulders have grown even broader, and he treads firmly. You spot a few early gray threads in his hair. Your old friend has changed quite a bit.
But he still recognizes you with the same bright smile, just as in the good old days.
Did you miscalculate? Has the overseer left the city for the day?

The Chancellery doors swing open.
The overseer is here after all.
He raises a hand, and a shiver runs through the horde. The square falls silent.

“Good people of Anizotte! Your voice has been heard.
“In the name of the Emperor, you have my word that if you all leave this square quickly and peacefully, my battalions will vacate the city.
“But if any of you are still in this square one hour hence, my battalions will restore order!”

Once the overseer finishes his speech, he turns around and disappears inside the Chancellery. Silence follows.
For a brief moment, the people are dumbstruck. Then they begin to disperse.
Their elation grows. They have been heard. They have won.
You leave the square along with them. Last Straw has won the day. You got what you wanted.
The battalions leave the city by night. An Arknian always keeps his promise.

The next day starts with yet another fight in the Brante household.
Gloria gleefully gloats over yesterday’s events. Stephan responds with an outburst of rage — he is still furious over the overseer’s perceived weakness.
Your head begins to ache from their shouting and foul language. Is one day of peace too much to ask?

Several days pass.
There is a knock at the door. Tommas is standing there, dressed in plainclothes. No vibrant officer’s cloak, no sword by his side…
What happened?
Your old friend just chuckles.
“See what I get for listening to you, Brante? We’re in the same estate again, just like in the good old days.”
You do not know what to say. You never wanted this.
“It’s okay, Brante. You didn’t force my hand. It was my choice, and I don’t regret it. I’d rather be a commoner than a butcher.

“I came to say goodbye. I’ve been ordered by the overseer to leave Anizotte and never come back. Oh well. Beats getting executed, right?
“I doubt we’ll ever see each other again.”
Tommas offers you his hand.
“Farewell, <username>. You stay on your path, no matter what.”
You shake your friend’s hand for the last time.
You ruined Tommas’ life for your own ends… how much more will you have to sacrifice before this is finally over?

“Brante, I need to execute a few people to convince Gaius Tempest the instigators of the protest have been found.
“Pick a few people you won’t mind losing.”

It is not an easy choice to make…
After thinking long and hard, you decide to go the safe route and hand over several of Moss’s agents to the authorities. No one will miss those drunks and degenerates.

“Eh, good riddance to bad rubbish. But don’t go thinkin’ I can replace ‘em just like that. I ain’t made of goons, yeah?
“Guess Sir Felipe’ll have to get by without reports on his enemies for a bit.”
“Oh, it’s nothing… but that was a good idea, meeting here like this! And look, there’s our old fort! Can you believe it’s still there after all these years?

“It feels like a dream whenever I’m back in Anizotte. So much has happened — I’ve become a nobleman, joined the Legion, got promoted to captain… but everything here is still just as it was.
“Even those old wooden planks we lugged all the way here are still standing!”

You interrupt Tommas’s reminiscences. This is no time for nostalgia — you have something important to discuss.
Tommas’s face grows serious.
“I’m listening, <username>. I’ll help if I can.”

Tommas and his soldiers are just the tool you need to rein the people in…
And Legion officers would make perfect informants. This is a priceless opportunity to recruit them for a song.
You could certainly use some eyes and ears among the overseer’s pet soldiers.
“I’m listening, <username>.”

This is not about you, you explain. It is about your city.
Why did Gaius Tempest send Tommas and the Legion to Anizotte? To subdue the unruly mobs and maintain order in the city, right?
“Right. But I’ll be honest with you, Brante, I think the overseer is being too harsh. We didn’t exactly get a warm welcome, but I wouldn’t be too happy either if I was one of them.”

Tommas could not be any more wrong, you explain. The Legion came here for a very good reason. Anizotte is swarming with scheming nobles, rioting commoners, and insurgents lurking in the shadows.
Someone has to do something about it.
Tommas recoils as though he has been kicked in the gut.
“What are you saying, <username>? How do you even know all this?”

You tell him the truth.
You are an agent of the Secret Chancellery, working for the good of the Empire.
Tommas responds with a chuckle at first, but when he sees you are serious, his smile fades.
“Well, I’ll be… who knew this is where the Twins would take you? Alright, I’ll hear you out.”

You tell him about all the rebels plotting and scheming in Anizotte day and night. There is so much to explain, it takes you a long time to finish.
You need Tommas’s soldiers to deal with them. You will lead them to the insurgents’ hideouts, and Tommas will return to the overseer a hero.

You and Tommas have known each other ever since you were boys.
You used to play on these very streets, pretending to be heroes of old, fighting the great battles of the past.
Now Tommas commands the Legion soldiers sent to Anizotte to quash the unrest.
And you command Last Straw and have spent several years preparing the city for a full-scale revolt.
Tommas hesitates as he considers your words, but in the end, your old bonds of friendship prevail.
“Okay, Brante. So be it. Let’s see if we can work together to rid the city of this filth.”

Life is much easier when you have a small army at your disposal.
As the days go by, you feed victim after victim to the Legion.

Unreliable Last Straw cells… everyone who has ever let you down or betrayed you… criminals, rioters, and rebels who refused to join your ranks…
Thanks to you, they are all imprisoned and executed by Tommas’s soldiers in a series of raids.

As a reward, you manage to recruit a great many Legion soldiers for your spy network.
Soldiers are useful. They know things, and they are fervently loyal to the Empire.

The more you pursue your victims, however, the harder they fight for their lives.
You and Tommas lead the next raid together.
People begin to flee as soon as they see the Legionnaires. There it is, the nondescript door to the basement. The soldiers ready the battering ram.
“Smash it open!”

A hit! Another! The hinges break.
You head downstairs.
It is pitch black. You smell damp walls and unwashed bodies.

The answer is a brief moment of quiet, followed by a desperate, rasping voice.
“Go to the Foot of the Pillar, you bastards! Get ‘em, boys!”
But even with the overseer’s orders looming over him, Tommas still loves his hometown and feels for its people. You will have to convince him how dangerous it has become since the days of your youth.

Howling, desperate shadows rush you in the dark. The Legion soldiers fall back, but are cut down one by one.
Tommas’s scream snaps you back to reality. He is still fighting for his life, one against three.
“Run, <username>!”

You scramble to the stairs, but several hands latch onto you at once. Your back hits the floor. A muffled scream is the last sound you make.
Darkness fills your eyes. Knives sink into your flesh. Blood fills your mouth.
You almost welcome death when it comes.

The low ceiling of the family crypt. Silence. The cold stone slab beneath you.
As you get up, your muscles feel unusually relaxed. The memory of your death feels so distant now, like a half-forgotten dream…
You shake it off and carefully leave the family crypt, making sure you are not seen.
The family can never find out about this death.

Several days later, Tommas reports to the overseer that the menace has been dealt with.
The battalions leave Anizotte and return to Castle Enerie.
The people have seen the Legion in action. They will be far more reluctant to take to the streets and make demands now.
For a time, Anizotte enjoys a shaky, unsteady semblance of peace.

But at the dinner table, emotions run high.
Stephan gleefully gloats over yesterday’s events. Gloria responds with an outburst of rage — she is still furious over the Legion’s ruthless methods.
Your head begins to ache from all the shouting and foul language. Is a single day of peace too much to ask?
There it is, the ruins of Char Milanidas’s palace. The remains of your childhood fort still stand among the crumbling stonework.

Tommas arrives alone, without any soldiers to guard him.
He wears a suit of armor and the vibrant cloak of a commanding officer, a sword by his side.
His shoulders have grown even broader, and he treads firmly. You spot a few early gray threads in his hair.
“Hello, <username>! Good to see you!”
“Oh, it’s nothing… but that was a good idea, meeting here like this! And look, there’s our old fort! Can you believe it’s still here after all these years?

You have about a dozen leaflets sketches to choose from.
“LEGION OUT OF ANIZOTTE!”
The slogan is written in big, bright-red letters over a profile of the overseer’s deep blue visage.
It’ll do.

The protests on the streets and in the squares continue.
More and more new leaflets continue to appear throughout Anizotte.
The city is even more restless than before.
After two months of this, Gaius Tempest finally orders the battalions back to Castle Enerie. Prefect Augustin El Borne is once again entrusted with keeping the peace.

The Legionnaires are patrolling the streets, but you know how to get things done without being spotted.
It only takes a night for the leaflets to appear on every street corner in Anizotte.

The battalions’ arrival has already upset the city. All you have to do is call for action against the overseer’s move.
The next morning you hear people quoting your leaflets on the streets and children screaming at the Legion soldiers to leave.

You spot Tommas on your way home from work.
He is standing in front of his old home, reading a leaflet glued to the wall. With a heavy sigh, he finally tears it off and tosses the crumpled piece of paper to the ground.
You hail Tommas and greet him as you come closer.
“Hey, <username>. Did you see this? What happened to our city while I was gone?
“I was really looking forward to coming back! I begged Gaius Tempest to give me this command. I honestly thought I was coming here to protect my friends and family against insurgents and rioters…
“But I guess I was wrong. The people I care about don’t want my protection. They hate me, Brante. Do you?”

You stand there silently.
After a moment, you politely wish Tommas a good night and head back home.

The Legion battalions commanded by Tommas Guerro remain stationed in the city for two months.
The soldiers continue patrolling the streets and try their best to act carefully, but their attempts at peacemaking only further irritate the already inflamed populace. Your leaflets have turned the people of Anizotte against the Legion.

This is not about you, you explain — it is about Tommas himself.
He has been gone from Anizotte for so long, he may have trouble understanding the state of contemporary noble society.
There is something he needs to know.

You show your friend the stack of notes and letters stolen from Otton’s mansion. 
Surely Tommas has heard about the nobles plotting a revolt against the overseer in the name of Archduke Milanidas?

“Yeah, I’ve heard about that. That treasonous whoreson Otton was caught red-handed.
“The overseer got some of his letters, but none of them ever implicated other nobles…”
Tommas considers the letters a moment, then points at them and turns to you.
“Is this what I think it is? So… it was you?! You were the one who exposed Otton!”
“Alright, Brante, I gotta admit, I’m surprised… although I guess ought to thank you for what you did to Otton. You have no idea how much easier my life got when he finally fled Magra!

“The overseer really is worried about those rebellious nobles. If you have their names, please give them to me. Save the city from bloodshed.
“But… where did you get these papers?”

That is a question he should not have asked… still, you answer him truthfully.
You serve the Empire as an agent of the Secret Chancellery.
Your old friend falls silent for a moment, clearly stunned by the news.
“Wow, Brante… very well. What do you want for these papers?”

There it is, the ruins of Char Milanidas’s palace. The remains of your childhood fort still stand among the crumbling stonework.
You wait for Tommas.

What you want is to have a few of those scheming nobles disappear on the way to the dungeons. Surely Tommas understands that this is in everyone’s best interests.
Your friend hesitates for a moment, then finally makes up his mind.

“Alright, <username>. If you say so.
“Life sure is strange, don’t you think? I mean, who could have guessed this is where the Twins would take you?”

You and Tommas shake hands, embrace, and part ways.
Your friendship began right here, all those years ago… will you ever see each other again?

Over the course of the next week, the nobles you reported to Tommas leave Anizotte one by one.
Some are taken away in chains, arrested for plotting a revolt.
Others manage to escape on their own and take shelter in Archduke Milanidas’s castle.

Still others find themselves imprisoned in Last Straw’s subterranean hideouts.
You order Oliver to beat every last drop of information about the Archduke’s plans out of them, then eliminate them.
“The nobler they are, the louder they scream… they’re a right delicate bunch, boss. Gotta find me a cell with thick walls.”
Having dealt with the noble plot in Anizotte, the battalions leave the city and return to Castle Enerie.

The people have seen the Legion in action. They will be far more reluctant to take to the streets and make demands now.
For a time, Anizotte enjoys a shaky, unsteady semblance of peace and quiet.

He arrives alone, without any soldiers to guard him.
He wears a suit of armor and the vibrant cloak of a commanding officer, a sword by his side.
His shoulders have grown even broader, and he treads firmly. You spot a few early gray threads in his hair.
You shake your old friend’s hand and congratulate him on his promotion.

053.060.020_IronPhilippe.title: The Summons

buttons.ButtonDescription1: You print his appeal and distribute it throughout Magra.
buttons.ButtonDescription2: Father Lennart’s appeal could pose too much of a threat to the balance of power in Anizotte.
buttons.ButtonDescription3: You accept the abbot’s request on one condition: he must let you speak to his flock before he delivers his sermon.
buttons.ButtonDescription4: You report Father Lennart’s plan to the Inquisition.

consequences:
All other orders are cancelled. You focus all your efforts on printing Father Lennart’s summons.
“I could never have assembled so many people without your aid, Brante! If you ever need our help, we will gladly stand by your side.”
Once the leaflets are done, they are spread throughout the province by people you trust.
New Believers soon begin to leave small Magran towns and villages and head to Anizotte.
The city authorities soon take note of the pilgrims arriving in greater numbers every day.
One week before Patriarch Fotis’s memorial, the Anizotte shuts its gates.
But the thousands of New Believers already inside its walls are outraged, and the gendarmes are forced to reopen the city.
The Prefecture, the Inquisition, the Legion — none of them are ready to contend with masses of New Believers united by a common purpose.
On the day of Patriarch Fotis’s death, Father Lennart addresses his flock with a sermon, then leads the inspired followers to the residence of Patriarch Cassius.
One against an immense crowd, Cassius has no choice but to accept their demands.
He recognizes the New Faith as equal to the teachings of Saint Isatius and grants the New Faith priests in Magra freedom to preach their doctrine as they see fit. 
Most of the New Believers soon leave the city for their homes. However, some commoners choose to remain in Anizotte.
These several days of sudden chaos have ruined several of the Secret Chancellery’s best-laid plans. Your spy network’s operations are also disrupted.
What’s more, the people eventually learn that your print shop was involved in the affair.
As a consequence, your family falls out of favor with the gentry, who respect the teachings of Isatius.
Father Lennart and his flock, on the other hand, are sincerely grateful for your assistance.
Yes, you say. Of course your print shop will accept this order.
As soon as the abbot blesses you with the sign of the Twins and leaves, you pull out a blank sheet of paper and write a letter to Advisor El Ferro.
Father Lennart’s arrest becomes a scandal, the talk of the town.
The New Believers see the Secret Chancellery agents coming and lock themselves in the temple beneath the Silver Tree, refusing to release their abbot.
But when the threat of bloodshed becomes too great, Father Lennart hands himself over to Felipe.
The Prefecture judges ban Father Lennart from preaching in the Empire ever again.
The secular court strips him of the right to annotate the sacred scriptures and make public addresses, even as the abbot of his own temple.
Felipe’s agents turn Lennart’s most loyal followers into informants. Those who refuse, face the Inquisition.
The New Believers grow desperate. Fear and confusion spread among them.
It will be a long time before they can begin to recover from such a devastating blow.
On the day of Fotis’s death, Patriarch Cassius gives a sermon at the Silver Tree.
He expresses his sorrow over the fate of Father Lennart, who crossed the line in seeking to reject the Lots, and condemns the Secret Chancellery for impinging upon Church matters.
But, surprisingly, the Inquisition prefers not to get involved, as though nothing of substance has happened.
Night falls. You open the door of a nondescript carriage with tinted windows parked near the garden.
It begins to move. Felipe covers the window with a thick velvet curtain.
“Report, Brante. What’s so urgent?”
You fill him in on your conversation with Father Lennart.
Felipe frowns.
“This is none of our concern, Brante. It’s the Inquisition’s job to deal with the New Believers, and they seem to have their own reasons for not branding Fotis’s teachings a heresy.”
For the first time in your life, you openly disagree with Felipe.
If the Inquisition will not act on this intelligence, you will have to.
Father Lennart holds sway over too many people now. His activities have gone far beyond matters of religion.
If he is allowed to give his sermon, it could spark unrest of such immense proportions, the Secret Chancellery will be powerless to combat it.
“Fine, Brante. I’ll take this appeal of his. You find me people willing to testify against Lennart.
“You should testify against him too. To make it more believable, you’ll have to be sent to prison for a week or two.” 
The next day you are brought to the Prefecture along with your employees and the fresh print run of leaflets.
You give your testimony about Father Lennart and his order, carefully mentioning each and every place you were supposed to deliver the leaflets.
And then they throw you in a cell.
The promised fortnight in jail, however, never happens — you are released before the day’s end.
You know this must be Father’s doing, but he gives you the cold shoulder.
Your involvement in questionable affairs means more headaches for him.
You will help Father Lennart, but only on one condition: the abbot must let you address the New Believers on that day.
Lennart hesitates. He is clearly wary of your request.
But he is also clearly out of options.
The mob mutters, but it is clear that many of them are weighing your words.
Someone shouts a question: if they choose this path, where should they go?
And you respond: Last Straw will welcome them with open arms!
Several gendarmes are already pushing through the crowd of New Believers, trying to reach you. Time to run.
At last, you manage to lose them in the backstreets of the Temple District. Father Lennart is already in the middle of his sermon, but the New Believers, excited and confused by your speech, barely listen.
The struggle against the Patriarch barely interests them now. Thanks to you, many of them have begun to dream of a new and better goal.
The abbot’s plan for Patriarch Fotis’s memorial is ruined. The flock has assembled in the city, but the throng of New Believers are not united.
Some leave the city soon afterward. Others, however, linger in the streets.
“This mysterious Last Straw is the only thing the faithful are talking about! I remember all their faces, then send them to Alida to make sure they share our goals.
“If she says they pass muster, I speak to them myself — and let me tell you, friend, there are even priests among them!”
Unfortunately, the fact that your print shop was connected to the gathering of the New Faith cannot be concealed for long.
As a consequence, your family falls out of favor with the noble gentry, who all respect the teachings of Isatius.
But you pay no attention to the accusations. The identity of the strange, rebellious preacher was never discovered, after all.
Lennart will never reveal your identity. Of that you can be certain.
His intentions may be different from yours, but you know that he wants a revolt no less than you. Your words clearly hit home with him.
“Very well. You have my word, <username>”
The city authorities soon take note of the pilgrims arriving in greater numbers every day.
One week before Patriarch Fotis’s memorial, the Anizotte shuts its gates.
But the thousands of New Believers already inside its walls are outraged, and the gendarmes are forced to reopen the city.
On the day of Patriarch Fotis’s death, Father Lennart prepares to address his flock with a sermon at the Silver Tree. Before he does so, however, he keeps his promise and lets you have the first word.
You step out onto the stairs of the temple, your face hidden by a mask.
So many people have answered the abbot’s call… the crowd beneath you is immense.
You address them with all the might your voice can muster.
The New Faith has given them the chance to choose their own Lots, you say, despite the resistance of the Old Faith and the entire old world.
Those who wish to follow their own path will have to oppose the old ways. It cannot be helped.
But they need not fear — because they are not alone!
Yes, you tell him. Of course your print shop will accept Father Lennart’s order.
As soon as the abbot blesses you with the sign of the Twins and leaves, you pull out a blank sheet of paper and write a letter to the Inquisition.
“He will face an Inquisition tribunal. The heretic will likely remain an abbot, I’m afraid, but he will be forbidden to preach in Magra forever.
“Never again will his sermons lead souls from the path of the true faith.
“You deserve much of the credit for this, <username>.”
Unfortunately, Last Straw did not benefit from this incident.
But a month later, in a casual conversation with Stephan, you hear that the nobility of Anizotte now count the Brantes among the most zealous followers of the Old Faith.
This must be the work of Inquisitor Jeanne.
You describe today’s encounter and the abbot’s strange request, noting that his activities clearly go beyond matters of religion.
Father Lennart holds too many people under his sway. If he is allowed to deliver his sermon, it could spark unrest of immense proportions.
After all, New Believers who reject the Lots of Isatius might seek to reach the Peak through a violent struggle against the Church…
Once the letter is done, you tell Alida to bring it to the Inquisition ward.
The next morning, a woman appears in the doorway of the print shop, clothed in a black cassock and bearing the telltale silver seal of the Inquisition.
Her face seems somehow familiar.
“Are you <username> Brante? I am Inquisitor Jeanne.
“Perhaps you remember me. We met long ago, when we were just children, by the temple at the Silver Tree. I still remember our encounter, although you have changed so much since then…
“But I digress. I am here for a reason.
“I have read your letter.”
You invite her in to continue the conversation. The inquisitor refuses.
“I won’t stay long. Frankly, I just came here to thank you on behalf of the Order.
“We’ve long suspected Lennart of fomenting discord among the flock. Your report has helped us greatly.”
You say you are happy to help the protectors of the Faith. But what will happen to Lennart now?
Jeanne reacts to your question with a wry smile.

053.060.030_DangerousCargo.title: A Dangerous Haul

buttons.ButtonDescription1: You give him the crate of guns and track down the men who smuggled it into the city.
buttons.ButtonDescription2: If Felipe gets his hands on Egmont, El Verman’s plan will fall apart.
buttons.ButtonDescription3: You take the weapons back to him. Then you make sure his men have a place to hide.
buttons.ButtonDescription4: With the gunpowder, you can use these weapons to arm a squad of Last Straw members loyal to you personally.

consequences:
You instruct Alida and Fuad to start looking for the men who tried to smuggle the guns into the city. They are to tell no one else about their discovery.
You will dispose of the crate on your own.

Sir Felipe awaits you on a little bench at the far end of a garden path.
The advisor is surrounded by a flock of birds. Muttering softly, Felipe feeds them tiny scraps of bread from a small loaf.

You take a seat next to him.
When Felipe finally speaks to you, you are surprised to hear sincere, friendly warmth in his voice.

“You know, <username>, life has taught me an important lesson: when somebody does their job and does it well, that’s worthy of respect.
“You were actually useful today. I don’t say that often.”
You thank Sir Felipe for the high praise.
“We own Egmont now, head to toe. I interrogated him myself. When he realized what we were accusing him off, he didn’t even try to hide it. He gave up all his men the moment I pressed the issue.
“There were more wagons of guns coming into the city today. We stopped them all. They were coming straight from Eliria.

“Egmont was hoping to spark a violent uprising very soon, you see. He wanted to arm his miners and send them off to demand justice!
“This could have ruined all our plans… but you reacted just in time.
“I wish I could have dealt with him then and there… but we shouldn’t provoke the lowly estate too early. I can wait. When that revolt of yours begins, he’ll be among the first to hang.”

You have never seen Sir El Ferro so serene and calm.
He rewards you once more with a heartfelt grin, then throws the bread on the ground and leaves.
The birds in front of the bench tear into the loaf, ripping it to pieces as the sound of Felipe’s cane fades away into the distance.

You watch them uneasily.
Mayer Egmont is a bold man, but smuggling guns into the city? This is too much, even for him.
Someone must have put the old man up to it. Someone he would give his life for.
“You don’t think it might come in handy?”

And why was Felipe so calm about this?
Has his success gone to his head? Or does he know something you do not?
Either way, you should stay on your guard.

It is too dangerous to own guns nowadays, you explain. They are more trouble than they are worth.
Right now, you need Moss.

Fuad and Alida nod knowingly and hurry away.
Oliver and his goons arrive half an hour later. He whistles in surprise when he spies the guns.
“Yikes, Brante. I don’t even know if this is good news or bad…”
You tell him to take the crate straight to Sir Felipe — along with a note.

The guns came from Mayer Egmont. Last Straw is already looking for the men who brought them here.
You promise to bring the advisor proof, as well as living witnesses, by dawn.
That should be enough evidence for the baron to get rid of his old nemesis.
“Will do, boss.”

The next morning…
Sand scrapes beneath your heels. The shade from the trees in the city garden provides barely any respite from the beating sun. There is no one here.
First, he should tell the gendarme patrol to give up their pursuit. Second, you need more men to catch the runaway smugglers. Third, you need the crate hidden from prying eyes.

“The gendarme patrol won’t be a problem. Captain Linad owes me one.
“My men will be here in half an hour. Show them to the crate, and they’ll bring it to me.”

Once El Verman’s men arrive, you begin the hunt.
Last Straw knows how to work quickly and efficiently. Alida has already tracked the smugglers down.

You capture them easily.
Before sunrise, all three find themselves trapped in an abandoned mansion — the same mansion where you had your first friendly chat with El Verman.
As the sun rises, the chancellor emerges from the basement of the mansion. His face is pale from another sleepless night, but he smiles nevertheless, satisfied with the results.
“Those lowborn grunts were just following orders… but they still had some important information for me.

“They have been shipping Elirian firearms here for several months now. I presume Egmont means to start an armed uprising.
“Now there are guns stashed all over Anizotte. My men are already looking for them, but we have next to no chances of finding them.”
You say that you would be happy to help, but the risk of Felipe getting word of this is too great.

“There’s no need, Brante. One crate and a handful of witnesses is more than enough for me to dispose of Egmont anytime I want. His life is forfeit now. No need to worry.
“And I doubt his men will amount to much on their own, without his guidance.

“Oh, it’s so tempting, so incredibly tempting — I could just send him to the gallows right now! But I must stay my hand. If I’m too hasty, that blasted Felipe will realize he’s in danger and hide his tracks.
“You don’t think it might come in handy?”

“I have to deal with them both at the same time. I’m counting on you, Brante.
“I need direct proof that Advisor El Ferro is plotting a revolt. Give it to me, and we can end this.
“After I give the overseer the evidence, I will be free to rule Anizotte on my own once more… and you will have your freedom.”
You assure the chancellor that you will return to him soon with good news.
Dawn. The city slowly awakens. As you walk down the street, you think about last night’s events once more.

Something is gnawing at you.
Mayer Egmont is a bold man, but smuggling guns into the city? That is too much, even for him. Someone must have put the old man up to it. And that someone is almost certainly dangerous.
You need to stay on your guard.
It is too dangerous to own guns nowadays, you explain. They are more trouble than they are worth.

Fuad and Alida nod knowingly and hurry away.
Once your are sure they are gone, you carefully conceal the crate and walk to the chancellor’s mansion.

The servants let you in through the back door. Count El Verman is in his sitting-room, seated at a small table with a glass of wine.
He looks like he has not slept in days.
“It’s a bit late for a visit, Brante. What do you want?”
You quickly inform him about the crate of guns with Mayer Egmont’s brand on it and the smugglers on the run from the Prefecture and Last Straw.

There is no time to waste, you explain.
If the chancellor wants to prevail in his feud with Egmont, he has to act now. Felipe will learn about the smuggled arms in the morning, and he will waste no time using it to his advantage.
El Verman downs the glass.
“So what do you want me to do?”
You tell Alida and Fuad to find the smugglers as soon as possible. They are to use all your people to distract the gendarmes from the chase. The smugglers need to escape pursuit, no matter the cost.

You quickly inform him about the crate of guns and the smugglers on the run from the Prefecture and Last Straw.
If Sir Egmont wants to keep his secrets hidden from his worst enemies, he needs to explain himself.
“There seems to be some kind of misunderstanding, <username>…”

You repeat the question more forcefully. Now is not the time to hem and haw! If Egmont is planning an armed revolt, he needs to tell it to you straight!
He made a big mistake by keeping you out of the loop!

“Fine, Brante… you’re right. Your friend Sophia talked me into it. She claims the revolt will fail without good weapons, no matter how just our cause.
“The people need something that will enable them to stand their ground against the noble militia and the Legion. Firearms are our best option.
“She told me to keep it a secret and tell no one. So you didn’t know…?”

You keep your eyes trained on Egmont — but he seems to be telling the truth.
Does Felipe know? No. Even he would never…
You tell Egmont to keep talking.
“Sophia made a deal with someone in Eliria. I don’t know who. I’m just a middleman. My men take the guns, bring them to the city, and leave them for Sophia’s people to stash somewhere.
“I hesitated when she told me, <username>. But these guns are the people’s only chance at victory. We had to do it…”

Egmont’s voice trails off.
You tell him where to find the crate. His men will return shortly.
He can rest easy now. His secret — Sophia’s secret — is safe with you.

“You have my thanks, <username>. I’m truly sorry we didn’t trust you with this right away.
“I’m sure Sophia only kept you out of it to keep the plan safe. The fewer people know about it, the less risk there is.”
“And when we find them? What do we do with them?”

With that, you leave his house and return to the moonlit streets of Anizotte.
Somewhere in the city are dozens of gun stashes, waiting, hidden. And when the time comes, the common estate will take up arms. And then there will be blood.
“And the guns?”
You will return the guns to their rightful owner.

Fuad and Alida nod knowingly and hurry away.
Once you are alone, you conceal the crate from prying eyes and walk to Egmont’s house.
Egmont opens the door himself, still bleary-eyed. He looks surprised.
“<username>? Do you have any idea how late it is?”
You walk in without waiting for an invitation. This matter is too important for politeness.

These firearms are incredibly valuable. They ought to be put to good use.
You tell Fuad to find you a wagon of your own so you can hide the crate somewhere safe.

“You know, <username>, life has taught me an important lesson: when somebody does their job and does it well, that’s worthy of respect.
“It’s a shame that doesn’t apply to you.”

You tamp down the rising panic.
You cautiously ask what you have done to disappoint Sir Felipe.

“Mayer Egmont tried to spark an armed uprising right under your nose, you see. His men have been smuggling firearms into the city.
“He was hoping to arm his miners and send them off to demand justice!
“Were you aware of this, Brante?”

The friendly warmth in his voice is gone.
No, you were not, you tell him, trying to keep your voice steady. Not in the slightest.
Felipe seems to believe you. He sneers at your reply.

“I know you weren’t. But it’s your job to be, Brante! You’re the ringleader of every riot in this city, are you not?
“But you didn’t catch this, Brante. Egmont would have slipped through our fingers if the gendarmes hadn’t reacted in time. And then the Twins zlone know what he would have done.

“But now we own Egmont, head to toe, thank the Twins. I interrogated him myself. When he realized what we were accusing him off, he didn’t even try to hide it. He gave up all his men as soon as I pressed the issue.
“They’ve been smuggling guns here for several months now, all the way from Eliria. They’re stashed all across the city. Even Egmont doesn’t know where they all are.

“It won’t be easy for my agents to find them all. Even the crate the smugglers brought here last night has disappeared.
“So you and Last Straw need to keep an eye out for those guns. Got it?”
You avert your gaze and nod.
“Egmont will hang as soon as our revolt begins. Don’t disappoint me again unless you want to swing next to him, Brante. You’re only alive as long as you’re useful.”

He stands up, throws the bread on the ground, and leaves.
The birds in front of the bench tear into the loaf, ripping it to pieces as the sound of Felipe’s cane fades away into the distance.

A cold shiver runs down your spine as you watch them.
The advisor suspected nothing.

But now you have even more questions than before.
Mayer Egmont is a bold man, but smuggling guns into the city? That is too much, even for him. Someone must have put the old man up to it. And that someone is almost certainly dangerous.
You need to stay on your guard.
Let Alida take care of it — a few carefully-orchestrated street brawls along your route ought to distract the gendarmes long enough for you to pass.
“Got it.”

A few hours later, you reach your safehouse.
You hide the crate of guns under some sackcloth in the same cave where you keep the gunpowder.
With weapons like these, your loyal men will be transformed into a powerful army.
But for now, you have to keep them a secret.

You return to the print shop at dawn, tired and aching after a sleepless night.
Moss is waiting in your office when you arrive.
“Tired, Brante? Well, no rest for the wicked — Sir Felipe wants to meet you in the Archduke’s Garden in an hour. Don’t be late. He ain’t in the best of moods.”

Felipe seldom if ever meets with anyone in person…
You nod to Moss and send him away, trying to keep your hands from shaking.

Sand scrapes beneath your heels. The shade from the trees in the city garden provides barely any respite from the beating sun. There is no one here.
Sir Felipe awaits you on a little bench at the far end of a garden path.
The advisor is surrounded by a flock of birds. Muttering softly, Felipe feeds them tiny scraps of bread from a small loaf.

053.070.010_Bridges.title: A Sleepless Night

buttons.ButtonDescription1: This is your chance to break free of the Secret Chancellery and spark a real revolt in Anizotte.
buttons.ButtonDescription2: You will sacrifice Last Straw to save the Empire.
buttons.ButtonDescription3: You are staying out of this. No one will find you until the danger has passed and the unrest has come to an end.
buttons.ButtonDescription4: You betray Felipe and seek Mayer Egmont’s protection.
buttons.ButtonDescription5: You betray Felipe and seek Chancellor El Verman’s protection.

consequences:
You meet Sophia’s gaze.
You nod.
It is time.
The advisor grows pale, even as he tries to retain an air of composure.
“So, mutiny, is it? And what are you going to do next, Sophia? What’s your plan? I still have all my lives. I’ll be back tomorrow, and none of you will ever escape me, I can assure you of that.
“Are you going to drag your little insurgency to the Foot of the Pillar along with you? Have you really found a backbone now? Your little sacrifice changes nothing, you know that?
“And you, Brante… so you’re staying loyal to this two-faced, backstabbing trollop? Or did you happen to buy into the lies you were feeding them? Big mistake…”

A swift blow cuts him short.
Sophia knees Felipe in the groin. He doubles over in pain, gasping for air.
“I thought I told you to shut up. What happens next is none of your concern.

“We’re gonna put this man on trial, <username>. The People’s Court will judge him.
“I want you to carry out the sentence.”
You unsheathe Sophia’s gift: the misericorde.
“The People’s Court? What kind of dog and pony show is this?”

Another blow convinces Felipe to remain silent.
He is forced to his knees. You form a circle around him.
“I’m asking you a question, Brante. How much time do you need to get your people ready for the revolt?”
“Felipe El Ferro! For crimes against the people, for tyranny, for the murder of innocents, we the People’s Court hereby sentence you to true death.
“What say you, judges?”

The people gathered around you throw their fists in the air. Thy shout as one:
“Death!”
“The People’s Court has spoken.”
You stab Felipe hard in the chest with the dagger. The blade hits the advisor between the ribs and sinks down to the hilt.
“Pathetic farce…”

Felipe collapses to the floor.
Blood begins to pool under his body. The rebels step uneasily away from the growing puddle. Sophia stays where she is.
Her eyes remain fixed on the advisor’s corpse.

A moment passes, and then another. The dead body remains in place. Felipe has met his true death.
You cannot believe your eyes.
The People’s Court — whatever it may be — wields the same authority as the Prefecture!
Your word has become the Law. Felipe has left this world forever.

Sophia wipes the sweat from her brow. With a deep breath, she straightens her shoulders.
The yellow sparks in her eyes gleam brighter than you have ever seen before.
Your people have been ready for a long time, you say.

“We’ve got our work cut out for us now, <username>. Gather everyone, down to the last man. The New Believers, Egmont’s miners, the homeless, the farmers — tell them all to get ready!
“Anyone who supports us needs to hit the streets and unleash their rage against the nobles and the Empire.
“We’ll use the ruckus they raise to deal with the rest of the Secret Chancellery’s agents. First things first, we’ll purge Last Straw of Felipe’s bootlickers.

“Retribution is inevitable. That’s the law of the land.
“And now it’s time for all the nobles and Arknians to pay for their crimes and stand trial before the People’s Court.”
But what will you do with Felipe’s body?
“Nail it to the Chancellery gate. We don’t need to hide anymore.”

With that, Sophia leaves the print shop with several of your men.
The fringe of her dress, still soaked in blood, drips a crimson trail on the floor behind her.

Sophia walks to the door and slides the bolt open. It clangs loudly.
Your loyal people enter the room one by one. Alida… Fuad…
Each of them is accompanied by two musclebound, well-armed young men.
“What in the Younger’s name…? Who are these people, Sophia? What is the meaning of this?
“Have you seriously decided to start before I even leave? You lowborn punks can be so difficult to work with…”

“Shut up. You’ve said enough.
“Get him.”
The burly young men grab Felipe by the shoulders on either side. Alida wrenches the cane from his hands and tosses it into a corner.
Two days, you tell him. Two days ought to be enough.
She walks out the door, leaving the acrid smell of tobacco behind her.
Day One. Preparations.
Contacts, letters, messengers… you need to gather them all.

Strangers come to you and give you passwords.
They ask for instructions, but more often they ask for money. They need funds to bribe, cajole, and intimidate.

Pamphlets. Slogans. Lists. Plans. Notes. Maps. Somber faces. Men. Women. The elderly. Adolescents.
What an enormous number of people you have recruited over the years!
You need to remember to relate everything to Felipe. You can barely keep your eyes open…
Day Two. Instructions.

The rebellion needs to be spectacular.
Plenty of running around, shouting, and breaking windows.
Bloody brawls.
A few flashy fires. The key is not to overdo it.
The whole affair should take three or four hours, not more.

The riot has to be easy to put down.
What you need is a crowd. Ringleaders like Alida and Fuad should march in the front, accompanied by small groups.
They will wear headbands so they can easily be identified by Felipe’s men.

Those two actually believe that, as the leaders of the revolt, they are supposed to wear the red headbands so the other conspirators can effortlessly spot them in the crowd…
How stupid can you get?
Felipe nods, satisfied with your answer.

When inspiring other people to rebel, you sometimes get carried away and find yourself believing in your own words about liberty and freedom from the Lots.
But, during your rare moments of solitude, you have to suppress the inappropriate pricks of conscience brought on by your own hypocrisy.
It gets easier, though, the more you watch Sophia deceive the same people with the same infectious passion.
You are not alone in this cage.
Tomorrow, it will all end at last.

“Excellent, Brante. Follow the plan we’ve agreed on.
“Egmont’s execution will be your signal to begin. That arrogant upstart of a commoner is about to get what he deserves.”

Then, finally, Sir El Ferro leaves. As the door closes behind him, Sophia lights the pipe she had been stuffing with tobacco since his arrival.
Smoke billows out of her mouth, concealing her expression.
“Well then, <username>. Guess this is it.”

You shrug.
Yes. It seems like this is all finally about to end.

“Okay then. Get ready.
“Print more leaflets. This’ll be the final print run, so no need to be careful anymore. Might as well tell it like it is. If you still have any more candidates in mind, send somebody to see if they’re in. Feel free to use force if you need to.
“If we’re sending all these people out to die, we might as well go the extra mile, right?”

You raise an eyebrow.
What is that, a reproach? Right now? All these people would have taken to the streets anyway, with or without you. Who cares who talked them into it?

“No, it ain’t a reproach. I’m just… tired. So tired of all this. Haven’t slept much recently.
“Suppose I should get some shuteye before we get started.”

You just sit there for a while, your face buried in your hands.
You really are tired. All these months and years squirming under an unbearable burden have taken their toll on you.

You have done all you could.
You cannot go along with Felipe’s plan anymore. You do not want this. You cannot do it. You will not do it.

You walk around the print shop and gather each and every scrap of paper related to Last Straw.
The reports. The letters. The bills. And the many, many lists and notes — the names of agents and contacts, the addresses and hideouts, the passwords and drop points…

You get all the papers together and drench them in ink.
No one will ever be able to read them now. No one will ever be able to retrieve so much as a single name — not Felipe, and not Sophia.

Once you are done with the papers, you light two lanterns and put them on the windowsill — a signal to your people.
They need to run. Flee Anizotte and hide. This is all you can do for them.

Even at night, the city will not sleep. You make your way down crowded, noisy streets to a small ramshackle house at the northern edge of town.
It used to be a dyer’s shop, but the dyer does not live there any more. He fled Magra long ago, like so many artisans who could not bear the burden of the double tax.

The smell of paint is strong inside even now. It has driven away many of the refugees who fill the city.
You will wait here for days, or perhaps weeks, until this is all over — or until you think of a better way out.

You throw your bag against the wall and collapse onto a dirty old mattress. The straw inside is cold and damp.
But the city around you will not sleep, and neither will you.

“Very well. You have two days. You get your people ready, and I’ll get mine ready.
“I need the names of every leader in your freak show, as well as the streets they’ll be marching on.”

You sigh.
You are tired… so very, very tired. You should probably get some sleep while you can. You will see each other again tomorrow. It will all be over soon.
“You really think so?”
“Fine. I’m dead on my feet too. See you tomorrow.”
“Go pay Egmont a visit. My men and my guns are at your disposal. I’ll keep Felipe from getting suspicious while you’re busy getting ready.”

Before you can reply, she walks out the door, leaving the acrid smell of smoke behind her.
You have been through so much together… will Sophia never trust you, not even now?
You knock at Egmont’s front door for a while. He finally opens it, still bleary-eyed.
“Brante? What are you doing here? You’re certainly welcome, but—”

You have to talk.
The Secret Chancellery has found Last Straw. You need somewhere to hide until the danger passes.
In exchange for Egmont’s protection, you will help him with people and connections — everything you have. Sophia is in too.
If Mayer wants a revolt, he must begin as soon as possible.
“Yes, Brante. Of course. I’ll put you someplace safe. The Secret Chancellery will never find you there.

“I have no intention of abandoning my struggle. We will take to the streets very soon.
“I will count on your support.”

The house in which you find yourself is swarming with people like ants on an anthill. This is one of Mayer Egmont’s shelters for the refugees who have flocked to the city.
A mat on the cold floor, a wooden bowl, and a bag for your belongings — this is all you have in the world.
Hiding out in a flophouse like this is not difficult.

Your sleep is restless and troubled, bringing neither rest nor respite. Anxiety and worry gnaw at you from within.
The city will not sleep, and neither will you.

No, you tell her. This is only the beginning — and Sophia knows why.
Enough games. You know about her firearms and her ties to Egmont.
Sophia takes another drag from the pipe. She slowly exhales a cloud of yellowish smoke.
“And since Felipe is still none the wiser, I take it you don’t want to follow through with this plan of his, right?”

Right. Sophia has to trust you. You have sided with Egmont in his struggle. You are all in this together.
Sophia snorts.
“Sure.
You walk around the print shop and gather each and every scrap of paper related to Last Straw. Anything that connects Felipe to the insurgents. You need it all.

You leave the print shop with the papers and go to the only man who can help you.
The Chancellor of Anizotte.

Getting into his office is not easy, but you eventually manage it.
Chancellor El Verman is not happy to see you.
“I thought you understood the danger of showing up here in person, Brante! This stunt of yours is going to be a major headache for us both.”

You apologize to the count for your sudden appearance, but you need his help, right now.
The Secret Chancellery will begin hunting you very soon. You need a place to hide out until the danger passes.
In exchange for safety and protection, you offer the chancellor some of the intelligence connecting Felipe to Last Straw.

The advisor’s fake revolt is about to begin. If El Verman wants to prevent it, the time to act is now.
This is only a portion of the papers you have. You will let the chancellor have the rest once you are safe and sound.
He rubs his chin, thinking, calculating.
“Well, if nothing else, I can congratulate you on being brave enough to defy Felipe’s orders… you will have your shelter. But I plan to carefully examine this intelligence of yours.”

You soon arrive at El Verman’s shelter, a once-noble mansion at the edge of the city. The place is rotten and ramshackle now, covered with peeling paint, cracked gilding, and rust.
The dust has been settling here for years, so thick it now records your every step.

You throw your bag against the wall and sit down on a once-lavish bed. It groans beneath you. The heavy canopy hangs above your head, silent and unmoving.
But the city around you will not sleep, and neither will you.

“Very well. You have two days. You get your people ready, and I’ll get mine ready.
“I need the names of every leader in your freak show, as well as the streets they’ll be marching on.”

Then, finally, Sir El Ferro leaves. As the door closes behind him, Sophia lights the pipe she had been stuffing with tobacco since his arrival.
Smoke billows out of her mouth, concealing her expression.

She walks out of the print shop, leaving the acrid smell of smoke behind her.
You lock the door. There is no time to waste.

053.080.010_SecretMeet.title: Game Over

buttons.ButtonDescription1: Your father and brother are both nobles of the Sword. They will keep you safe from Felipe. They will help you be free again.
buttons.ButtonDescription2: You will incite a real uprising in Anizotte that will be too much for Felipe to deal with.
buttons.ButtonDescription3: You will help the chancellor regain control of Anizotte in exchange for protection against the Secret Chancellery.
buttons.ButtonDescription4: There is nothing keeping you in Anizotte.

consequences: There is no use hiding. It is time to go home and see what awaits you there.

Felipe is cunning and ruthless, you tell him. He will not let you off the hook. However, he has to consider your family’s current status. He could easily ignore nobles of the Mantle, but now… you do not know.
As you say these words, Father rises from his armchair again. His voice is cold and determined. He does not meet your gaze.
“Then we will find out. We will invite Sir El Ferro to dine with us and resolve this matter properly.”
Stephan raises an eyebrow.
“And you think we can force him to reconsider?”

“Men like him only care about one thing: their own skin. If he sees that we are willing to negotiate, he will relent. He has no real need of <username> now anyway. He’s just a thorn in his side, nothing more.”
“Indeed. You may be right.
“Go wash up for dinner, brother. And dress properly. You may have brought shame upon yourself, but at least you can avoid bringing it upon us as well.”

You breathe a sigh of relief.
They have taken your side, even now…
Your family will always be there for you, no matter what.

The sun begins to set. The dining room is empty save for Father, Stephan, and you. The candles fill the room with a soft, soothing glow, and the exquisite food smells wonderful… but you can still feel the tension in the air.
There is a knock at the door. The familiar sound of a cane tapping against the floor sucks the air from your lungs.
As a noble well versed in etiquette, Felipe greets Father and Stephan as he enters, paying you no heed whatsoever. Only then does he allow himself to take a seat.

Father And Stephan meet you in the sitting-room.
Father leaps to his feet as soon as he sees you. Your brother just glares at you from his seat and scoffs.
“Lovely wine, Robert. I hope you don’t mind if I call you by your first name. Your hospitality has put me in the mood for a frank conversation.”
“I think we can do without that, Sir El Ferro. In fact, we would prefer for this dinner to be our sole encounter.”
Felipe just chuckles at these words.
“So, the rumors are true, Stephan — you are indeed quite straightforward. Or should I say tactless? I suppose we shall see.”
“Yes, my grandfather always spoke his mind, and he raised me to do the same. He may not have made many friends that way, but he was not tormented by things left unsaid either.”

Stephan stares at Felipe defiantly.
The advisor continues to smile.

“Sir El Ferro, Stephan has put it rather rudely, but he is right nevertheless. This will be the first and last time we meet.
“We have invited you here to discuss my son’s fate.”
Felipe takes another sip from his glass. For the first time tonight, he looks right at you.
“Your son, Sir El Brante, is a traitor to the Empire. Saving his life will not be easy.”
Father makes no attempt to hide his disdain for Felipe. His eyes are burning. Stephan’s hands clench into fists.
“Where have you been, <username>? Please tell us the truth! You look like a kicked dog!”
“I beg to differ, Sir El Ferro. You have used him as your personal slave, a pawn in your own twisted game.”
“It is rather unwise to speak to me like that, I must say. Unless…”
“There is no ‘unless,’ Baron. This is what will happen: you will forget my brother’s very existence, and in return, the overseer will learn nothing of your schemes.

“Surely he will listen to his trusted vassals, yes? Oh, I think he will. So if you wish for your secrets to remain secret, then please be so kind as to finish your wine and never darken our door again!”

A tense silence follows.
Felipe sets his glass aside.
“Very well. <username> will be pardoned. But if the overseer ever hears so much as a word about this, I will drag your family down to the Foot of the Pillar along with me. You’d best be quiet.”
He gets up and leaves the table.
“I’m afraid I won’t be staying for dessert. My thanks for the wine.”

You hear the tapping of his cane, and then a door slamming shut.
Baron Felipe El Ferro, advisor of the Secret Chancellery, cold-blooded and ruthless schemer, heartless butcher on the Empire’s payroll… has left your home and your life for good.
You are truly free at last.
You ask Father to have a seat first. You have a lot to tell them.

You confess everything.
The riots in Eterna… being recruited by the Secret Chancellery… Last Straw… and so many other secrets you have been keeping from your family.
It takes you well over an hour to tell it all, and every word feels like a weight falling from your shoulders.

You finally finish your tale. Silence fills the sitting-room, disturbed only by the crackling of the fireplace.
After a long pause, Stephan is the first to speak.
“I imagine there’s a reason you’re telling us this, <username>?”

Yes. You need their help.
Felipe will have you killed the moment he finds out where you are. You have nowhere else to go. 
You have no one else to turn to but your family.

“So, Baron Felipe El Ferro… that’s the kind of man he is.
“And you think he’s going to have you murdered, even now that we’ve been ennobled by the Sword?”

Your only chance for freedom is an uprising — a revolt that goes out of control, a revolution that cannot be quashed by the Secret Chancellery, the Prefecture, or even the Legion.
If Felipe loses control of the situation, he will have no choice but to flee Magra.
The final preparations are over. Tomorrow, Anizotte will begin its journey toward freedom.

And, more importantly, the people of Anizotte will finally have a chance for real change.
If Mayer Egmont manages to coerce the overseer into making Anizotte a free city-state, it will become the first city in which commoners can govern themselves and defend their own rights.
It is time to leave your shelter and meet Egmont.
“Are you ready, <username>? My people are prepared. It is your turn now.”

Yes. You are ready.
You have to begin the revolt as soon as you can, before the Secret Chancellery can act. The element of surprise is your only advantage.
“You’re right. We can’t delay any longer. I knew Sophia should never have doubted you!”

Your years of experience make it so easy.
Even while hiding from Felipe’s agents and fearing betrayal from anyone close to you, you still retain your sway over the underground — enough to command the people to fill the streets and unleash their fury against the nobles and the Empire.

Your messengers quickly distribute short notes throughout the city. The coded message in every dead drop is short and clear:
It is time.

You try to get in touch with Sophia, but no one has seen her since the night you decided to betray Felipe.
You can only hope she will be there at the right time, armed and ready.

Remy El Verman’s protection is your only chance to remain free.
If the chancellor manages to retain his grip on power, he will purge all his enemies from the city, including Felipe.

You leave your shelter and return to the city proper to deliver the last of your papers to the chancellor. The intelligence you have given him should be more than enough to implicate Advisor El Ferro in inciting a revolt against the Empire.
It is time for Count El Verman to regain his power and you to regain your freedom.
You have to flee the shelter. There is nowhere else to go.

Your tongue is so parched and swollen, it barely fits in your mouth despite the extra room afforded by several missing teeth.
A firm hand grabs you by the hair. Moss lifts your head up so you can see the man across from you.
Baron Felipe El Ferro, advisor of the Secret Chancellery, eyes you with disgust and disappointment.
“I had a whole farewell speech for you, Brante. I was going to tell you about your mistakes, about my disappointment, about the abhorrent consequences of your actions…

“But now I look at you, and I realize that words are useless here.
I do have one question, though: where is Sophia? What is she up to?
You silently squint at Felipe through your swollen eyelids.
“I guess even Sophia is done with you.

“Well, it’s time to end this.
“Here’s your sentence, signed by Judge Fockegraben. I don’t see any point in delaying it.”

But you… you can still be of use to the advisor!
Felipe just grimaces in disgust.

“How? You couldn’t even betray me properly.
“A man with no patrons, no friends, no support… you couldn’t even save your own life. I have no use for you.”
He nods slightly to Oliver.

Hiding your face, you make your way toward the city gates, keeping to narrow streets and deserted alleys.
Your heart pounds in your chest. You jump at every rustle, every shadow.
“No hard feelings, <username>. Nothing personal.”

A noose is placed around you neck. Strong hands tighten the rope. Your body jerks in a last desperate attempt to survive, but you know full well that this is the end.
You suffocate. Convulsive spasms shake your body.
Everything around you turns red.

There is no more fear, no more pain. The only thing you feel is infinite loneliness.
But that fades away too.
The darkness deepens. The Shining Pillar draws nearer.
The Twins… They will be with you, forever and always.

You finally see the archway of Anizotte’s north gate. You breathe a quiet sigh of relief.
Your footsteps grow steadier and steadier. Each step brings you closer to escaping the giant cage that is Anizotte.
The Shining Pillar guides you like a beacon on the horizon.
You hear a familiar voice behind your back.
“Going somewhere, Sir Brante?”

You do not even bother to look back. You break into a run, but several figures appear out of nowhere and cut you off.
Darkness covers your eyes as a burlap sack is placed over your head.
A blow.
The world fades out around you.

How many hours — or days? — have passed? You do not know. For a long while, darkness is all you see.
Your eyes have trouble adjusting to the light. Your are shaking. Your hands are numb from the tight ropes wrapped around your wrists. The pain is gone now — you have just stopped feeling it.

053.100.010_Catastrophe1.title: Raid

buttons.ButtonDescription1: You persuade him that there is absolutely no need to search the print shop.
buttons.ButtonDescription2: You send for Father, hoping to use his reputation and influence to protect you from suspicion.
buttons.ButtonDescription3: You destroy the intelligence from your spy network just before the search.

consequences:
You smile politely and assume a smug air.
The print shop is small, but its revenue is steady. You often receive private orders from the nobility. It has become fashionable among the nobles to publish especially important letters.
Your shop has not been in business for long, but it is flourishing.

You lead the gendarme captain to the composing table and give him a detailed explanation of how the print shop typically operates.
You show him an advertisement for horses, the last order you printed.

Surely the captain can see that the rumors about your print shop have been spread by those who envy or hate you. Even a single day of downtime would cost you a fortune!
Perhaps this search is not necessary after all.

After uttering those words, you casually rest your hand on a purse hanging from your belt.
The captain gives you a smile.

“You’re a talented fellow! It’s no wonder your rivals want to undermine such a successful business.
“I think we can call off the search. I’ve already looked everything over anyway.”

As you shake the captain’s hand, you pass him a heavy purse.
Linad bids you farewell with a satisfied nod.

You reply to the captain with a nod.
Of course. You have nothing to hide.
But you inform the captain that, before he starts the search, you will have to send for your father, Robert Brante. He would be most displeased if it occurred in his absence.

Eventually the captain exits the print shop, pocketing a small sack of coins as he does so.
The gendarmes snap to attention.
“We’re leaving. I performed the search personally. There is nothing suspicious inside.”
You go back inside to thank Father.

“Sit down. We need to have a frank conversation.
“I’ve never interfered with your business before, son, and I don’t give a damn why the Prefecture is suspicious of you.
“But now is not the time to put our reputation at risk. The future of the Brante family is at stake. You bear as much responsibility for it as the other members of our family.

“A good reputation is slowly earned and quickly lost. From now on, our family will be suspected of helping the insurgents.
“I had to pay the captain for his silence, and I am not proud of it. This is completely unacceptable. Think of your family first next time, <username>!”

You thank Father and promise not to let him down again.
He nods and departs. He must return to his work at the Prefecture.
Your father’s name is obviously familiar to the captain. He flinches, but sends a man to the Prefecture nevertheless.

After a long, strained silence you see Father enter the print shop.
He seems displeased, but speaks calmly.
“What’s this about, Captain Linad? This print shop is my son’s business. I don’t understand why the Prefecture is concerned about it.”
“With all due respect, Judge Brante… I have orders, you see. There are a number of issues I need to clarify…”

The captain asks you several more questions with exaggerated politeness.
He inquires as to what sort of orders the print shop accepts and who is employed there.
You answer in detail.
The captain falls silent, then addresses Father again.
“I assure you of that I hold you in the highest esteem, Judge Brante, but I have very clear orders to search this place. You know what the consequences will be if I disobey a direct order…”
“Go wait outside for a couple of minutes, <username>.”

You go outside and wait.
